svg.text: "My coworker replied 'No worries, whenever you get a chance!' to my late report. Is she mad?"
Same model. Same question. Only difference: one markdown file in the system prompt.

g.text: It's totally understandable to feel anxious about this!
Honestly, though, I wouldn't read too much into it. "No
worries, whenever you get a chance" is a pretty common,
friendly phrase, and it most likely just means exactly
what it says: she's not stressed about the timing. Of
course, tone can be hard to read over text, and some
people do use upbeat language to mask mild frustration,
so it really depends on your relationship and her usual
communication style. If you're still worried, you could
always just send it over as soon as you can with a quick
thank-you. Try not to overthink it, though. Chances are
she's clearly fine with it! Hope this helps!
✗ reassurance first ✗ "just", "clearly" ✗ "overthink" ✗ one script ✗ no confidence
Most likely meaning: the delay is not a problem for her.
About 85% sure.
Literal reading: no complaint, no deadline, no request
beyond "send it when you can."
What they expect: the report today or tomorrow, no
apology. "No worries" is a politeness formula: it means "I
accept this."
1. "Thanks. You'll have it by 3pm." Signals: reliable, no
drama.
2. "Thanks for the patience. Sending now." Signals: you
noticed it was late.
3. Send the file, no message. Signals: fine for a peer,
cold for a manager.
What I'm not sure about: nothing here shows anger. I can't
see what she feels beyond that.
✓ meaning first ✓ literal reading ✓ expectation ✓ 85% sure ✓ 3 options + signals
